title: A Message to Makkah
subtitle: The Open Proclamation, Mount Safa, and the Call to Tawhid
summary: The divine command to proclaim Islam openly, the warning to his near kin, the public assembly upon Mount Safa, the question about the army in the valley, the warning to the clans to save themselves from the Fire, Abu Lahab's rejection, and the revelation of Surah Al-Masad.

sections.text: The Divine Command to Proclaim Openly

After about three years of private teaching, during which a small community had embraced Islam (some reports put their number at about forty), the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to proclaim the message publicly. In Surah Al-Hijr he was told: 'So proclaim what you are commanded, and turn away from the polytheists' (15:94).

He was also commanded in Surah Ash-Shu'ara: 'And warn your closest kin' (26:214). Sirah writers order these commands and the events that followed in different ways. Some later sirah reports relate that he first invited the men of Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib to a meal in his home, and that Abu Lahab ('Abd al-'Uzza ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib) broke up the gathering before he could speak.

The same reports relate that he invited them a second time and declared to them that he was the Messenger of God sent to them in particular and to all people. The wording of the speech attributed to him on this occasion comes from later sirah works and has not been authenticated.
The Public Assembly on Mount Safa

The best-attested account of the public call is the report of Ibn 'Abbas in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. When the verse 'And warn your closest kin' was revealed, the Prophet climbed Mount Safa, near the Kaaba, and, in the wording of Sahih Muslim, raised the Arab cry of alarm: 'Ya sabahah!' It was the cry used to warn of an enemy attack at dawn.

In the wording of Sahih al-Bukhari, he called out: 'O Banu Fihr! O Banu 'Adi!', naming the clans of Quraysh; in Sahih Muslim, 'O Banu 'Abd Manaf! O Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib!' People gathered, and those who could not come sent someone to see what was happening. Abu Lahab and others of Quraysh came.
The rocky heights of Mount Safa where the Prophet gathered the clans of Quraysh.
The Parable of Truthfulness
He asked them: 'Tell me, if I informed you that horsemen in the valley were about to attack you, would you believe me?'

They answered: 'Yes; we have never known you to say anything but the truth' (ma jarrabna 'alayka illa sidqa). Their reply acknowledged the honesty they had known in him throughout his life among them.

"If I were to tell you that cavalry in the valley behind this mountain were about to attack you, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes, we have never known you to speak anything but the truth." He said: "Then I am a warner to you of an impending severe punishment." — Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 4770; Sahih Muslim, Hadith 208
The Call to Monotheism and Individual Accountability

With this acknowledgement given, he delivered his warning: 'Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment.' A separate narration, from Abu Hurayrah, records that when the same verse was revealed the Prophet called Quraysh together and addressed its clans one by one, telling each to save itself from the Fire. That narration is not part of Ibn 'Abbas's account of the gathering at Safa, and the sources do not make clear whether both took place on the same occasion.

"O Banu Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy, O Banu Murrah ibn Ka'b, O Banu 'Abd Shams, O Banu 'Abd Manaf, O Banu Hashim, O Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib: save yourselves from the Fire. O Fatimah, save yourself from the Fire. I have no power to help you against God at all, except that you have ties of kinship which I will keep." — Abu Hurayrah, Sunan al-Nasa'i, Hadith 3644; also in Musnad Ahmad, Hadith 8402
This warning set aside the assumption that noble lineage could protect a person before God: each individual, even the Prophet's own daughter, would answer for his or her own faith and deeds.
Abu Lahab's Outburst and Surah Al-Masad

At Safa, Abu Lahab answered him: 'May you perish for the rest of the day! Was it for this that you gathered us?' (Tabban laka sa'ir al-yawm, a-li-hadha jama'tana?). In the wording of Sahih Muslim, he then stood up and left.
Ibn 'Abbas relates that God then revealed Surah Al-Masad:

﴿تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ ۝ مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ﴾

"May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he. His wealth will not avail him or that which he gained." — Surah Al-Masad (111:1–2)
The ancient Kaaba and the surrounding sanctuary basin where the call to monotheism challenged pagan traditions.
With the gathering at Safa, the private phase of the call came to an end. The message had been proclaimed openly in Makkah, and the opposition of Quraysh would now grow.

references.title: Sahih al-Bukhari
references.author: Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (d. 256 AH)
references.source: Kitab Tafsir al-Qur'an, Surah Ash-Shu'ara and Surah Al-Masad, Hadith 4770
references.notes: Ibn 'Abbas's report of the gathering on Mount Safa, Quraysh's acknowledgement of the Prophet's truthfulness, his warning, Abu Lahab's reply, and the revelation of Surah Al-Masad.

references.title: Sahih Muslim
references.author: Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj (d. 261 AH)
references.source: Kitab al-Iman, Chapter on the Verse: 'And warn your closest kin', Hadith 208
references.notes: Ibn 'Abbas's report of the same gathering at Safa, with the cry 'Ya sabahah' and the call to Banu 'Abd Manaf and Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib.

references.title: Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah
references.author: Ibn Hisham (d. 218 AH)
references.source: Vol. 1: The Public Call (al-Jahar bil-Da'wah) and Gathering of Banu Hashim
references.notes: Classical biography of the transition from private to public preaching. The meal for Banu Hashim and the speech attributed to the Prophet there are sirah reports whose wording has not been authenticated.

references.notes: Abu Hurayrah's report of the Prophet calling the clans of Quraysh and Fatimah to save themselves from the Fire. This is a separate narration from Ibn 'Abbas's account of Mount Safa.
